note: Brook trout. Since 2026-09-28 the fins are not collected -- no fin outlines, bases or tips -- except the fin BASES, restored 2026-09-29/30: where each fin meets the body, which drying and pinning do not move -- the dorsal fin origin and insertion (its base endpoints), the pelvic base, and the pectoral insertion; the anal base endpoints and the pectoral ray tip were taken out again 2026-09-30. The dorsal base centre stays out: midpoints the endpoints make redundant. In these preserved specimens a fin's length and area record how it dried and was pinned more than its size, so the analysis (a size-corrected trait PCA, and a Procrustes analysis of the head) uses none of them. What is asked for is what that analysis uses: the snout, eye, jaw and gill cover points, the end of the vertebral column (caudal_base, SL's endpoint; the caudal crease points and the narrowest-peduncle pair were wiped from every fish 2026-09-30) -- the two mouth corners in the mirror, and both rulers. The 131 fish labelled before keep their fin coordinates in their sidecars; putting a fin back in scope brings its traits back. The body+caudal outline is not collected either, and Auto-label does not offer it: SAM wraps the adipose and anal fins instead of crossing their bases. The caudal points are placed by hand: Auto-label does not offer them (exclude_predicted_keypoints), its guesses there having been the least reliable.
